seed_commits.message:
chore: initial project scaffold

FastAPI service, Postgres in compose and the CI skeleton. No retrieval yet.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): hashed TF-IDF vectoriser standing in for an embedding job

A real deployment calls an embedding API. Doing that here would make the
corpus un-rebuildable without a key, the tests non-deterministic and the whole
thing dependent on a vendor being up.

The cost is semantics: only shared vocabulary brings two passages together, so
this behaves like good lexical search rather than a semantic retriever.
Dimension count and IDF weighting were both measured against the benchmark
questions rather than chosen.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): overlapping chunker

The overlap costs index size and buys one property: any two adjacent sentences
appear together in at least one chunk. Without it a fact stated across a
sentence boundary belongs to no chunk at all, so it is not ranked poorly -- it
is unretrievable at any top_k.
seed_commits.author: Dmitri Okafor <dmitri.okafor@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(corpus): the knowledge base

Twenty-seven documents across HR, IT, finance, security and engineering,
including three verbose policy pages that are eight times the length of a
handbook entry. That spread is why ranking has to normalise.
seed_commits.author: Dmitri Okafor <dmitri.okafor@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): the index, with two scores per hit

Cosine similarity ranks well and, because the space is hashed, invents
similarity for questions the corpus cannot answer. Lexical coverage compares
strings rather than hashes, so it cannot be fooled the same way. The router
needs both.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): refuse when the corpus has no basis for an answer

Measured on this corpus: out-of-corpus questions reach 0.181 cosine while
genuine ones go as low as 0.148, so no threshold on similarity alone separates
them. Coverage puts the out-of-corpus questions at 0.000. Requiring both is
what makes refusal reliable.

A refusal is a successful outcome, not an error, and the model is never called
for one.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(llm): recorded model client, keyed by question

Deliberately not keyed on the assembled prompt. The prompt embeds the retrieved
passages, so keying on it would make every retrieval change a cassette miss --
a retrieval bug would present as 'no recording found' rather than as the worse
answer it actually is.

The consequence, stated plainly: this cannot measure whether bad context
produces a bad answer. It measures everything the answer is built on instead.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): prompt assembly, trimmed by whole passages

Truncating mid-passage leaves it labelled and citable with half its text, so
the answer cites an id the model only partly read. The citation validates, the
audit trail looks clean, and the grounding is gone.
seed_commits.author: Dmitri Okafor <dmitri.okafor@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(rag): treat retrieved text as data and citations as claims

Anyone who can edit a page can address a sentence to the model rather than to
the reader, and retrieval will fetch it.

Quarantine is by document rather than by passage: chunking splits a page, so an
injected instruction lands in one chunk and the claim it is influencing lands
in the next. Withholding only the passage carrying the attack serves the rest
of the page, which is all the attacker needed.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(eval): four metrics and a labelled set

Each is a pure function over strings and ids, so each can be tested against a
constant worked out by hand.

Refusal correctness is balanced accuracy, never plain accuracy: the set holds
27 answerable questions and 7 unanswerable ones, as any real one would, and a
system that answers everything scores 0.794 plain against 0.500 balanced.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(api): ask, corpus and session history, plus the CLI

A refusal is a 200. The system was asked a question and gave its honest answer;
a 4xx would make a gap in the corpus look like a malformed request and would
put every one of them into the error rate.
seed_commits.author: Dmitri Okafor <dmitri.okafor@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: cover retrieval, routing, guardrails, assembly and scoring

Most of this suite needs no database and no network, and CI asserts that by
running it with both pointed at dead ports.

The baseline is 1.0 on all four metrics, deliberately: it makes every one a
regression test with nothing to argue about.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
ci: gate on the evaluation metrics, not just on the tests

Every metric is 1.0 on a healthy build, so CI can fail on any drop rather than
negotiating about what is good enough.
seed_commits.author: Ines Varga <ines.varga@example.com>
